content.title: About
content.content: Black toasted bread is a whole‑grain loaf made from rye and wheat, often sweetened with caramelized sugar or molasses, which gives it a dark color and a subtle sweet aroma. After baking, the slices are toasted until crisp, enhancing flavor and making them ideal for sandwiches and snacks.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Black bread is traditionally considered more nutritious than white bread because it contains more whole grains.
Toasting triggers the Maillard reaction, creating a characteristic caramelized taste.
In countries such as Russia and Poland, black bread is a staple and is frequently served with soups.
The dark color can be achieved by adding molasses or by a longer fermentation of the dough.
Toasted bread is often used as a base for bruschetta – open‑face sandwiches with various toppings.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Whole grains and bran in black bread provide a high amount of dietary fiber, supporting healthy digestion.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Sourdough fermentation preserves B1, B2 and B3 vitamins, important for metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The loaf supplies iron, magnesium and zinc, which aid immune function and energy production.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Thanks to whole grains and fermentation, black bread promotes satiety and causes a slower rise in blood sugar.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Caramelized sugars and whole grains contain polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Bread made from wheat and rye contains gluten, which can trigger reactions in people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High salt content
items.content: Some black bread recipes use a notable amount of salt; individuals with hypertension should monitor portion size.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Toasting adds a small amount of fat, so excessive consumption may lead to extra calorie intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Toasted black bread works well for sandwiches with cheese, ham, avocado or pâté. It can also be used for croutons, soup toppings, or as a crunchy side for salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the loaf in a paper bag or bread box at room temperature for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight bag; thaw and toast before use.
